doc.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 9, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Freddie Green's mysterious look
summary: Freddie Green once stopped playing and shook his head at the new drummer; other Basie drummers got the same look.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Freddie Green, the great Freddie Green, you know, the great guitarist, Mr. Time we called him, was on the band all his life practically. And I was new on the band. I’d been on the band a few months. And I was playing, I was learning the charts and things were going pretty good. And one night, which I have never ever forgotten, one night we’re playing and Freddie is sitting off just sort of a little bit off to my right. And suddenly he stops playing. He uncrosses his legs, puts his guitar down, turns around and looks at me, shakes his head, turns back around, re-crosses his legs, picks up his guitar and starts playing. To this day I have no idea what that was about. Ever. That was his version of “the ray.” Something was going on and Freddie was just making a statement.
Wow. Man that’s like, I mean you could go to bed for the rest of your life and go what was that, Freddie?

What did I do? But I do have to admit in all honesty, and I’m not going to name names, but I’ve talked with some of the other wonderful drummers that were in the band and they were all subject to Freddie Green turning and looking at them at one point or another. And maybe with the exception of Harold Jones, I don’t know, Harold never let anything get him down, with the exception of Jonesie I think all of us are still worried about whatever the hell it was the Freddie meant, all this time, all these years, what did he mean, what was I doing, oh my God. But I don’t know what it meant, Monk, I have no idea. But it sure messed my mind up for a long time.
